text:
Utah won 5-4, but the numbers say Toronto played the better game. TOR carried 3.01 expected goals to UTA's 2.45, and in simulated replays of every shot the Maple Leafs came out ahead 60 percent of the time. Two of Utah's five goals came on chances rated at 2 percent, and one of them was a shorthanded wrist shot from Mikhail Sergachev that made it 3-0 in the second period.

That stretch decided things. Daniil But opened the scoring late in the first, Vincent Trocheck made it 2-0 a minute into the second, and Sergachev's shorthanded goal three minutes later put TOR in a hole it never fully escaped. Auston Matthews answered on the power play, but Dylan Guenther scored on another 2 percent chance and MacKenzie Weegar added a late second-period goal to make it 5-2. At even strength the gap was real: UTA generated 2.03 expected goals to TOR's 1.1. Toronto's edge came from the power play, which produced 1.11 expected goals and two scores on five chances.

The Leafs spent the third period chasing. Matthews finished with a goal and an assist, and the line around him controlled the play, with Kirill Marchenko on the ice for 2.22 expected goals for and 0.17 against. John Tavares scored on the power play in the third, and Gavin McKenna's snap shot at 11:01 made it 5-4. Toronto never found the equalizer. Anthony Stolarz allowed 2.55 goals more than the chances against him suggested, and Karel Vejmelka was 0.99 below expectation but did enough to hold on.
